commitResults.messageTitle: Add skill field to Person model
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce a new Skill attribute and include it as a field in Person
to represent the client's skill level.

This allows the add command to store the skill level provided by
Trainers

commitResults.messageTitle: Add parsing support for skill parameter
commitResults.messageBody:
Update the parser to support the s/<skill level> parameter. The parser
extracts the skill level argument and validates that it belongs to
one of the allowed categories: pro, intermediate, or novice.

The add command currently does not recognize a skill parameter.
As a result, Trainers cannot specify the client's training experience
when adding a new person.

commitResults.messageBody:
The data load flow fails completely when the file contains invalid
entries. This prevents valid users from being loaded even when only part
of the file is corrupted, and makes recovery harder for the user.

The commit support partial loads by keeping valid users, extracting
invalid
entries to a separate file, and showing a startup warning when invalid
entries are skipped.

commitResults.messageBody:
This iteration tests the Timeslot class for errors, and fixes the issue
of SLOT_REGEX being misinterpreted as accepting timerange and slot number
separately in SINGLE_TIMESLOT_REGEX.

Previous iterations could not accept more than 1 edit to the timeslots
(i.e. can only edit 1 day at a time).

This causes inconvenience for the users as they have to edit day by day.

With this update, users can now all timeslots in one go, by splitting
days by a semicolon.
